The '''2024–25 [[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]] season''' was the club's [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|126th season in existence]] and their [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|94th consecutive season]] in the top flight. In addition to the [[2024–25 La Liga|domestic league]], Barcelona participated in this season's editions of the [[2024–25 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2025 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] (entering for the [[FC Barcelona in international football#European Cup / Champions League|21st consecutive season]]). The season covered the period from 1 July 2024 until 30 June 2025.

Barcelona played their official home matches at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]] throughout the season while awaiting the completion of renovations at [[Camp Nou]], which was not yet available at full seating capacity.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/noticies/3745829/el-projecte-de-lspotify-camp-nou-avanca-segons-els-terminis-previstos/amp |title=Spotify Camp Nou project going to plan |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=21 October 2023 |access-date=23 April 2024 |archive-date=11 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111050848/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/noticies/3745829/el-projecte-de-lspotify-camp-nou-avanca-segons-els-terminis-previstos/amp |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/mediterranean/20240419/9599102/barca-stadium-camp-nou-december-works.html |title=Barça wants to return to the Camp Nou on December 15th |publisher=[[La Vanguardia]] |date=19 April 2024 |access-date=23 April 2024 |archive-date=1 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101053035/https://www.lavanguardia.com/mediterranean/20240419/9599102/barca-stadium-camp-nou-december-works.html |url-status=live}}</ref> The club had initially planned to return to Camp Nou on 15 December 2024 but was unable to do so because UEFA regulations prohibited teams from changing venues midway through the Champions League league phase.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/barcelona-confirms-camp-nou-return-date-after-recent-delay |title=Barcelona Confirms Camp Nou Return Date After Recent Delay |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=20 November 2024 |access-date=21 November 2024 |archive-date=30 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130011300/https://www.si.com/soccer/barcelona-confirms-camp-nou-return-date-after-recent-delay |url-status=live }}</ref>

Barcelona won a domestic treble, defeating rivals [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in two finals and twice in the league to edge them out in the title race. Although Barcelona fell short in the Champions League, losing to [[Inter Milan]] in the semi-finals after extra time, the 2024–25 campaign was the club’s most successful season since [[2014–15 FC Barcelona season|2014–15]].

This was Barcelona’s first season since [[2009–10 FC Barcelona season|2009–10]] without veteran full-back [[Sergi Roberto]], who left the club when his contract expired.

The club is also connected to Coldplay through [[Viva la Vida#Sporting usage|the use of]] song "[[Viva la Vida]]" as the club's celebratory anthem since [[2008–09 FC Barcelona season|2008–09]].<ref>{{cite web|date=6 October 2024|title=Why Barcelona Will Wear Coldplay Sponsored Shirt Against Real Madrid|last=Bishop|first=Callum|url=https://www.givemesport.com/why-barcelona-will-wear-coldplay-shirt-against-real-madrid/|website=GiveMeSport|access-date=8 October 2024|archive-date=6 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241206001427/https://www.givemesport.com/why-barcelona-will-wear-coldplay-shirt-against-real-madrid/|url-status=live}}</ref> American rapper [[Travis Scott]] was announced as the team's sponsor for 11 May's Clasico and also performed an exclusive concert to promote the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-05-02/travis-scott-fc-barcelona-shirt-jersey-el-clasico/|title=Spotify and FC Barcelona Collab With Travis Scott on a Special Cactus Jack Shirt and Exclusive Concert|date=2 May 2025|access-date=3 May 2025|work=[[Spotify]] Newsroom|archive-date=7 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607022452/https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-05-02/travis-scott-fc-barcelona-shirt-jersey-el-clasico/|url-status=live}}</ref>|group=n1|name=jerseylogo}} / [[Philips|AMBILIGHT TV]] (left sleeve) / [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees|UNHCR – The UN Refugee Agency]] (back)

== Season overview ==

=== Background ===
{{See also|2023–24 FC Barcelona season}}

=== Pre-season ===
On 19 March, Barcelona announced they would be touring the [[United States]] to participate in the pre-season Soccer Champions Tour, with three friendly matches against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]] on 30 July, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey|New Jersey]] on 3 August and [[AC Milan|Milan]] in [[Baltimore]] on 6 August.<ref name="Pre-season1">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/futbol/primer-equipo/noticias/3936981/el-barca-visitara-de-nuevo-los-estados-unidos-en-pretemporada/featured|title=Barça heading to United States for another preseason|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=19 March 2024|access-date=24 April 2024|archive-date=24 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240424044437/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/futbol/primer-equipo/noticias/3936981/el-barca-visitara-de-nuevo-los-estados-unidos-en-pretemporada/featured|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Pre-season2">{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/when-do-real-madrid-and-barcelona-play-in-the-usa-in-2024-the-dates-of-their-preseason-tour-n/?outputType=amp|title=When do Real Madrid and Barcelona play in the USA in 2024? The dates of their preseason tour|publisher=[[Diario AS|AS]]|date=21 April 2024|access-date=24 April 2024|archive-date=24 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240424044435/https://en.as.com/soccer/when-do-real-madrid-and-barcelona-play-in-the-usa-in-2024-the-dates-of-their-preseason-tour-n/?outputType=amp|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 26 June, Barcelona announced that the pre-season would start with the players' medical examinations on 10 July.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/noticias/4045072/el-primer-equipo-masculino-volvera-a-la-actividad-el-10-de-julio|title=FC Barcelona first team back to work on 10 July|date=26 June 2024|access-date=11 July 2024|publisher=FC Barcelona}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/futbol/primer-equipo/noticias/4053664/asi-sera-la-primera-semana-de-la-pretemporada-del-fc-barcelona|title=Agenda for first week of preseason for FC Barcelona|date=8 July 2024|access-date=11 July 2024|publisher=FC Barcelona|archive-date=11 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240711023306/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/futbol/primer-equipo/noticias/4053664/asi-sera-la-primera-semana-de-la-pretemporada-del-fc-barcelona|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 June, [[Sergiño Dest]] left permanently for [[PSV Eindhoven]] on a free transfer, ending his four years at the club.<ref name="dest"/> Two days later, young striker [[Marc Guiu]] departed for [[Chelsea FC|Chelsea]] for €6 million.<ref name="guiu"/>

On 24 July, [[Pau Víctor]] joined Barcelona permanently, signing a contract until 2029.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4066407/pau-victor-blaugrana-until-2029 |title=Pau Víctor, blaugrana until 2029 |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=24 July 2024 |access-date=31 August 2026 |archive-date=18 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118200834/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4066407/pau-victor-blaugrana-until-2029 |url-status=live}}</ref> The following day, Barcelona opened preseason behind closed doors with a 1–0 win over Catalan side [[UE Olot|Olot]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/4067456/preparations-continue-with-olot-friendly |title=Preparations continue with Olot friendly |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=25 July 2024 |access-date=31 August 2026}}</ref>

On 30 July, Barcelona drew 2–2 with Manchester City in Orlando before winning 1–4 on penalties. Pau Víctor and [[Pablo Torre (footballer)|Pablo Torre]] scored the goals for Barça.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Dawson |first1=Rob |title=Grealish on target as Barca, City draw in Orlando |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/701275 |access-date=31 August 2026|date=31 July 2024 |work=ESPN}}</ref>

=== August ===
On 3 August, Barcelona defeated Real Madrid 2–1 in New Jersey. Pau Víctor scored a brace to secure the [[El Clásico]] victory.<ref>{{cite news|date=4 August 2024|title=Barcelona beat Real Madrid in New Jersey with Pau Victor double|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/701277|access-date=31 August 2026|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=1 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260901010746/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/701277|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, [[Oriol Romeu]] was loaned out to [[Girona FC|Girona]] for the rest of the season.<ref name="romeu"/>

On 6 August, Barcelona drew 2–2 with AC Milan in Baltimore before losing 3–4 on penalties. [[Robert Lewandowski]] scored both goals for Barça.<ref>{{cite news|date=7 August 2024|title=Christian Pulisic scores as AC Milan beat Barcelona in shootout|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/701279|access-date=31 August 2026|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=1 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260901074408/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/701279|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Barcelona announced reaching an agreement to sign [[Dani Olmo]] from [[RB Leipzig]] for a reported fee of €60 million on six-year contract, therefore the Spaniard completed a return move to his youth career club.<ref name="olmo"/><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Herrero |first1=Laia Cervelló |last2=more |title=Barcelona agree deal in principle for Olmo |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5620891/2024/08/06/barcelona-dani-olmo-transfer/ |access-date=10 August 2024 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=4 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250904025218/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5620891/2024/08/06/barcelona-dani-olmo-transfer/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 August, Barcelona lost 0–3 against [[AS Monaco|Monaco]] in the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]], failing to find the back of the net in their pre-season finale.<ref>{{cite news|date=12 August 2024|title=Barcelona trounced by Monaco in final game before start of LaLiga |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/715386 |access-date=31 August 2026|website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The next day, [[Julián Araujo]] was sold to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] for €10 million.<ref name="araujo"/>

On 17 August, Barcelona started the new [[2024–25 La Liga|league season]] on the right foot, with a 1–2 away win over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] thanks to a brace from Robert Lewandowski. [[Marc Bernal]] and [[Gerard Martín (footballer)|Gerard Martín]], and new signing Pau Víctor made their debuts.<ref>{{cite web|date=17 August 2024|title=Robert Lewandowski is deadly! Striker nets brace and 17-year-old Pau Cubarsi impresses in 2-1 win as Hansi Flick gets up and running in La Liga|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/lists/barcelona-player-ratings-vs-valencia-robert-lewandowski-pau-cubarsi-hansi-flick-la-liga/bltb9fbd8072159bd10#csa1c7094da9fe0f19|access-date=17 August 2024|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal.com]]|archive-date=18 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240818013437/https://www.goal.com/en-in/lists/barcelona-player-ratings-vs-valencia-robert-lewandowski-pau-cubarsi-hansi-flick-la-liga/bltb9fbd8072159bd10#csa1c7094da9fe0f19|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=17 August 2024|title=Valencia 1-2 Barcelona - Robert Lewandowski scores twice as Barca come from behind to win in Hansi Flick's debut|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/valencia-v-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10302703/story.shtml|access-date=17 August 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]|archive-date=28 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250228065230/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/valencia-v-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10302703/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 August, [[Ilkay Gündoğan]] left on a free transfer, returning to [[Manchester City]] after just one season at Barcelona.<ref name="gundogan"/> The next day, the team defeated [[Athletic Bilbao]] 2–1 in their first home match of the season, with Lewandowski and Yamal scoring a goal each.<ref>{{cite web|date=24 August 2024|title=Lewandowski strike hands Barcelona 2-1 win over Athletic Bilbao|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704672|access-date=24 August 2024|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=24 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240824193827/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704672|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 25 August, [[Mikayil Faye]] completed a permanent move to [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]] for €10.3 million.<ref name="faye"/> The next day, [[Vitor Roque]] and [[Clément Lenglet]] were loaned to [[Real Betis]] and [[Atlético Madrid]] respectively.<ref name="roque"/><ref name="lenglet"/>

[[File:Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys.JPG|thumb|right|[[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]] was used as the home ground for the second season in a row]]

On 27 August, Barça got a 1–2 comeback win away against [[Rayo Vallecano]] and climbed to first place in the league table.<ref>{{cite web|date=27 August 2024|title=Rayo Vallecano 1-2 Barcelona - Dani Olmo emerges from bench to rescue win for Barca on debut |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/rayo-vallecano-v-fc-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10313849/story.shtml|access-date=27 August 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]}}</ref> New signing [[Dani Olmo]] made his debut and scored the winning goal of the match, with the other goal coming from Pedri.<ref>{{cite web|date=27 August 2024|title=Dani Olmo scores winner on dream Barcelona debut in comeback win at Rayo Vallecano|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/cronica/2024/08/27/66ce0f88268e3e9c0e8b4593.html|access-date=27 August 2024|website=[[Marca (newspaper)|MARCA]]|archive-date=27 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240827214559/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/cronica/2024/08/27/66ce0f88268e3e9c0e8b4593.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=27 August 2024|title=A blow to the table! A comeback for the leader of a Barça led by debutant Dani Olmo (1-2)|url=https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/football-soccer/blow-to-the-table-comeback-for-the-leader-of-barca-led-by-debutant-dani-olmo-1-2_306843_102.html|access-date=27 August 2024|website=FCBarcelonaNoticias.com|archive-date=27 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240827214559/https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/football-soccer/blow-to-the-table-comeback-for-the-leader-of-barca-led-by-debutant-dani-olmo-1-2_306843_102.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day, [[Álex Valle]] was loaned to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] for the rest of the season.<ref name="valle"/>

Barcelona ended the month with a dominant 7–0 win against [[Real Valladolid]] on 31 August, making it four wins in four matches since the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=31 August 2024|title=Raphinha scores hat trick as Barcelona thrash Valladolid 7-0|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704692|access-date=31 August 2024|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=31 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240831183328/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704692|url-status=live}}</ref> Raphinha scored a hat-trick, with Lewandowski, Koundé, Olmo and Torres scoring a goal each, while Yamal contributed with two assists to continue his impressive start to the season. [[Sergi Domínguez]] also made his debut.<ref>{{cite web|date=31 August 2024|title=FC Barcelona 7-0 Real Valladolid: Magnificent seven|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4102104/fc-barcelona-7-0-real-valladolid-supersonic|access-date=31 August 2024|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=31 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240831183328/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4102104/fc-barcelona-7-0-real-valladolid-supersonic|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=31 August 2024|title=Barcelona 7-0 Real Valladolid: Raphinha, Robert Lewandowski & Dani Olmo among goals as Barca score seven|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/la-liga-live-barcelona-v-valladolid_sto10320548/story.shtml|access-date=31 August 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]|archive-date=31 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240831190051/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/la-liga-live-barcelona-v-valladolid_sto10320548/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== September ===
On 15 September, Barcelona defeated [[Girona FC|Girona]] 1–4, with Yamal scoring a brace and Olmo and Pedri scoring a goal each.<ref>{{cite web|date=15 September 2024|title=Girona 1-4 FC Barcelona: Five out of five|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4119416/girona-1-4-fc-barcelona-five-out-of-five|access-date=15 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=15 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240915162607/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4119416/girona-1-4-fc-barcelona-five-out-of-five|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=15 September 2024|title=Lamine Yamal Shows Potential to Become World's Best Player vs Girona |url=https://www.givemesport.com/lamine-yamal-shows-potential-to-become-worlds-best-player-vs-girona/|access-date=15 September 2024|website=GiveMeSport.com}}</ref> Lewandowski made his 100th appearance with the club.<ref>{{cite web|date=15 September 2024|title=Hundred appearances for Lewandowski with Barça|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4119215/hundred-appearances-for-lewandowski-with-barca|access-date=15 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=15 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240915231241/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4119215/hundred-appearances-for-lewandowski-with-barca|url-status=live}}</ref>

Barcelona started the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] campaign with a 2–1 defeat at the hands of [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], after [[Eric García (footballer, born 2001)|Eric García]] got sent off early on in the first half.<ref>{{cite web|date=19 September 2024|title=AS Monaco 2-1 FC Barcelona: Beaten with ten men|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4122766/as-monaco-2-1-fc-barcelona-beaten-with-ten-men|access-date=19 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=19 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919212654/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4122766/as-monaco-2-1-fc-barcelona-beaten-with-ten-men|url-status=live}}</ref> Yamal scored the only goal for the team and his first in the Champions League and became the second youngest goalscorer of all time in the competition, only behind his teammate Ansu Fati who holds the record.<ref>{{cite web|date=19 September 2024|title=Lamine Yamal makes history again|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4122787/lamine-yamal-makes-history-again|access-date=19 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona|archive-date=21 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240921025836/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4122787/lamine-yamal-makes-history-again|url-status=live}}</ref>

The team went back to winning ways after they defeated [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 1–5 to make it six wins in as many matches in the league. Lewandowski and Raphinha got a brace each and Pablo Torre scored once.<ref>{{cite web|date=22 September 2024|title=Villarreal 1-5 Barcelona: Robert Lewandowski and Raphinha fire braces in thumping win in La Liga|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/villarreal-v-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10345359/story.shtml|access-date=22 September 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]|archive-date=23 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923063222/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/villarreal-v-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10345359/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=22 September 2024|title=Villarreal 1-5 FC Barcelona: Unstoppable! |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4127461/villarreal-1-5-fc-barcelona-unstoppable|access-date=22 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona}}</ref>

Barcelona maintained their winning streak in the league when they beat [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] 1–0 on 25 September,<ref>{{cite web|date=25 September 2024|title=Barcelona maintain perfect LaLiga start with 1-0 win over Getafe|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704720|access-date=25 September 2024|website=[[ESPN]]|archive-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925212119/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/704720|url-status=live}}</ref> with the goal coming from Lewandowski who scored his 49th La Liga goal and became the league's all-time leading Polish goalscorer, overtaking the 48 goals scored by [[Jan Urban]].<ref>{{cite magazine|date=25 September 2024|title=Robert Lewandowski Breaks Jan Urban's La Liga Goalscoring Record|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/robert-lewandowski-breaks-jan-urban-la-liga-goalscoring-record|access-date=25 September 2024|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|archive-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925201706/https://www.si.com/soccer/robert-lewandowski-breaks-jan-urban-la-liga-goalscoring-record|url-status=live}}</ref> Lewandowski's goal also had special significance for the club, since with this goal Barcelona became [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|the first team in La Liga history to score 6,500 goals]].<ref>{{cite web|date=25 September 2024|title=Historical! FC Barcelona, 1st team to score 6,500 goals in LaLiga|url=https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/laliga/historic-fc-barcelona-1st-team-convert-6500-goals-laliga_307500_102.html|access-date=25 September 2024|website=FC Barcelona Noticias|archive-date=25 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925203202/https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/laliga/historic-fc-barcelona-1st-team-convert-6500-goals-laliga_307500_102.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Barcelona's perfect start of seven straight wins in La Liga ended after they suffered their first league defeat of the season, losing 4–2 away to [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]]. The goals for the team came from Yamal and Pau Víctor, who scored his first goal for the club.<ref>{{cite web|date=28 September 2024|title=Barcelona's perfect La Liga start ends with 4-2 defeat at Osasuna|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5801771/2024/09/28/barcelona-defeat-osasuna-la-liga/|access-date=28 September 2024|website=[[The Athletic]]|archive-date=29 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240929072001/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5801771/2024/09/28/barcelona-defeat-osasuna-la-liga/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== October ===
Barcelona started the new month with a 5–0 win against [[BSC Young Boys|Young Boys]] in a match where Lewandowski scored a brace, Raphinha scored once, [[Iñigo Martínez]] got his first goal for the club and the last goal of the match was an own goal scored by Young Boys' defender [[Mohamed Ali Camara]]. Young defender [[Andrés Cuenca]] also made his debut.<ref>{{cite web|date=1 October 2024|title=Barcelona 5-0 BSC Young Boys: Lewandowski at the double as Barca score five in thumping win|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2024-2025/barcelona-v-young-boys-uefa-champions-league-live_sto10356445/story.shtml|access-date=1 October 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]}}</ref>

On 2 October, Barcelona signed [[Wojciech Szczęsny]] to a contract until the end of the season after [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] suffered a severe [[patella tendon rupture]].<ref>{{cite news |date=2 October 2024 |title=Barcelona sign Wojciech Szczęsny after Ter Stegen injury |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/41437458/barcelona-sign-wojciech-szczesny-ter-stegen-injury |access-date=30 August 2026 |website=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=8 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250608152226/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/41437458/barcelona-sign-wojciech-szczesny-ter-stegen-injury |url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Barcelona defeated [[Deportivo Alavés]] 0–3 in their last match before the international break, with Lewandowski scoring his first hat-trick of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=6 October 2024|title=Lewandowski treble powers Liga leaders Barca to Alaves victory|url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/lewandowski-treble-powers-liga-leaders-161621158.html|access-date=6 October 2024|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]}}</ref>

After their return from the international break, the team continued their winning form by defeating [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] 5–1 on 20 October.<ref>{{cite web|date=20 October 2024|title=Barcelona 5-1 Sevilla - Robert Lewandowski and Pablo Torre net braces as Barca crush visitors in La Liga clash|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/barcelona-v-sevilla-la-liga-live_sto10370786/story.shtml|access-date=20 October 2024|website=[[Eurosport]]|archive-date=30 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241030183642/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/barcelona-v-sevilla-la-liga-live_sto10370786/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Lewandowski and Pablo Torre both scored braces, with Pedri scoring once.<ref>{{cite web|date=20 October 2024|title=Lewandowski and Torre at the double as Barcelona thrash Sevilla in LaLiga|url=https://www.flashscore.com/news/soccer-laliga-lewandowski-and-torre-at-the-double-as-barcelona-thrash-sevilla-in-laliga/p8lSTu1m/|access-date=20 October 2024|website=Flashcore.com}}</ref>

On 23 October, Barcelona defeated [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] 4–1 in a statement win and ended the six-match winless streak against the Germans.<ref>{{cite web|date=23 October 2024|title=FC Barcelona 4-1 Bayern Munich: Poetry in motion|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4154813/fc-barcelona-4-1-bayern-munich-poetry-in-motion|access-date=23 October 2024|website=FC Barcelona}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=23 October 2024|title=Barcelona is back. A Champions League conquering of Bayern Munich is the best proof yet|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-is-back-a-champions-league-conquering-of-bayern-munich-is-the-best-proof-yet-205522216.html|access-date=23 October 2024|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|archive-date=9 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260109173328/https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-is-back-a-champions-league-conquering-of-bayern-munich-is-the-best-proof-yet-205522216.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Raphinha marked his 100th match with the team with a hat-trick, with the other goal coming from Lewandowski.<ref>{{cite web|date=23 October 2024|title=Raphinha hat-trick inspires Barcelona to demolition of Bayern Munich|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/oct/23/barcelona-bayern-munich-champions-league-match-report|access-date=23 October 2024|website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

In the last match of the month, Barcelona demolished [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] 0–4 away in the first [[El Clásico]] of the season on 26 October.<ref>{{cite web|date=26 October 2024|title=Real Madrid 0 Barcelona 4 – Mbappe's Clasico to forget as Flick's team stun European champions|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5866056/2024/10/26/real-madrid-0-barcelona-4-mbappe-flick-lewandowski/|access-date=26 October 2024|website=[[The Athletic]]|archive-date=27 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241027114350/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5866056/2024/10/26/real-madrid-0-barcelona-4-mbappe-flick-lewandowski/|url-status=live}}</ref> Lewandowski scored a brace, while Yamal and Raphinha scored a goal each; with his goal Yamal became [[El Clásico#Other records|the youngest player to ever score in El Clásico]].<ref>{{cite magazine|date=26 October 2024|title=Watch: Barcelona's Lamine Yamal Becomes Youngest Goalscorer in El Clasico History|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/watch-barcelona-s-lamine-yamal-becomes-youngest-goalscorer-in-el-clasico-history|access-date=26 October 2024|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|archive-date=27 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241027121129/https://www.si.com/soccer/watch-barcelona-s-lamine-yamal-becomes-youngest-goalscorer-in-el-clasico-history|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=26 October 2024|title=Real Madrid's Galácticos humbled in El Clásico by Barcelona's bold trap and rampant attack|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/real-madrids-galacticos-humbled-in-el-clasico-by-barcelonas-bold-trap-and-rampant-attack-205253396.html|access-date=26 October 2024|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|archive-date=27 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241027162836/https://sports.yahoo.com/real-madrids-galacticos-humbled-in-el-clasico-by-barcelonas-bold-trap-and-rampant-attack-205253396.html|url-status=live}}</ref> With this win Barcelona ended Real Madrid's 42-game unbeaten La Liga run and defended their [[La Liga records and statistics#Streaks|record for the most consecutive league games without a loss]] in La Account as Los Blancos' Unbeaten Run Ends on Brink of History|url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2024/10/real-madrid-vs-barcelona-stats-lamine-yamal-first-clasico-goal|access-date=26 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241027120640/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2024-2025/real-madrid-v-barcelona-la-liga-live_sto10378143/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== November ===
Barcelona started November with a 3–1 win over [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in the [[Derbi Barceloní|Barcelona derby]] thanks to a brace from Olmo and a goal from Raphinha.<ref>{{cite web|date=3 November 2024|title=🚨 Barcelona secure comfortable derby win over Espanyol|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-secure-comfortable-derby-win-171600915.html|access-date=3 November 2024|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|archive-date=27 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227182335/https://sports.yahoo.com/barcelona-secure-comfortable-derby-win-171600915.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Later in the week, Barcelona won their third champions league match in a row defeating [[Red Star Belgrade]] in [[Belgrade]] with the score of 2–5 with Lewandowski scoring a brace and Raphinha, Iñigo Martínez and Fermín scoring each a goal. However, the Catalans' title hopes took a dent after a 1–0 away loss to [[Real Sociedad de Futbol|Real Sociedad]] and a 2–2 away draw to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]]. Barcelona then beat [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] 3–0 in the champions league to move into third place in the league phase table. November then ended with Barcelona losing 1–2 at home to [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] leaving them 2 points clear of 2nd-placed [[Atlético Madrid]] after 15 games.

=== December === 
Barcelona began December by beating [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] 1–5 away from home in the league. Their next game was a 2–2 away draw to [[Real Betis]] allowing Real Madrid to reduce their lead to two points. Barcelona would bounce back by beating [[Borussia Dortmund]] 2–3 away in the Champions League to move 2nd in the league phase table, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Barcelona's league title hopes were dented after a 0–1 home defeat to [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], but remained top of the league after Real Madrid drew their next game. However, Barcelona then suffered a late 1–2 home defeat to Atlético Madrid, meaning they would end 2024 second in the league.

===January===
Barcelona began the new year by defeating [[UD Barbastro|Barbastro]] 0–4 in the [[2024–25 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] round of 32, with Szczęsny and [[Toni Fernández]] making their debuts for the club. Four days later, they beat Athletic Bilbao 0–2 in the [[2025 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] semi-finals to set up a final with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].

In the [[2025 Supercopa de España final|final]] Barcelona beat Real Madrid 2–5 to win the Supercopa de España. Albeit a man down following the dismissal of goalkeeper [[Wojciech Szczęsny]], Barcelona came back from a goal down with four goals in a dominant first half at the [[King Abdullah Sports City|King Abdullah Sports City Stadium]] in [[Jeddah]], clinching the trophy for a record 15th time from the grasp of their fierce rivals.<ref>{{cite web |date=13 January 2025 |title=Spanish Super Cup: Barcelona defeats Real 5-2 in thriller Jeddah final |url=https://english.alarabiya.net/sports/2025/01/13/spanish-super-cup-barcelona-defeats-real-5-2-in-thriller-jeddah-final- |access-date=13 January 2025 |website=Al Arabiya}}</ref> The win also gave [[Hansi Flick]] his first trophy in charge of the club.

In the Copa del Rey round of 16, Barcelona beat Real Betis 5–1 at home to advance to the quarter-finals. They then played their first league game of 2025 which was a 1–1 away draw with Getafe. This crushed Barca's title hopes even more as they were now 5 points behind Atlético Madrid.

In the Champions League Barcelona faced [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] at the [[Estádio da Luz]]. Benfica took the lead in the 2nd minute through a [[Vangelis Pavlidis]] goal. Robert Lewandowski equalised from the penalty spot in the 13th minute before Pavlidids scored twice to put Benfica 3–1 up. Raphinha scored in the 64th minute to make it 3–2, but Araújo scored an own goal to make it 4–2 to Benfica. Lewandowski scored a pen in the 78th minute to give Barcelona hope before Eric Garcia scored in the 86th minute to make it 4–4. Raphinha then scored in the 96th minute to win the game 4–5 for Barcelona. The win confirmed Barcelona would finish in the top 8 of the league phase, earning automatic advancement to the Champions League round of 16.

Barcelona won a La Liga match for the first time in four attempts after beating Valencia 7–1 at home, to keep their title hopes alive despite being 7 points behind leaders Real Madrid.

Barcelona's final Champions League league phase match finished as a 2–2 draw against [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] on 29 January, which prevented the former from pipping [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to top spot in the league phase table; the club finished 2nd, two points off top spot. The next day, midfielder [[Unai Hernández]] was transferred to [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] for €4.5 million.<ref name="unai"/>

=== February ===
On 1 February, with his Celtic loan cut short, Álex Valle moved on a second loan to [[Como 1907|Como]] for the rest of the season.<ref name="valle2"/> The next day, Barcelona defeated Alavés 1–0, and with Real Madrid losing 1–0 to Espanyol, Barcelona reduced the gap between them and Real to 4 points.

Barcelona then won their Copa Del Rey quarter final against Valencia 0–5 to set up a semi-final with Atlético Madrid.

Barcelona won 1–4 against Sevilla in the league, and with Real Madrid dropping points again, closed the gap to Real down to 2 points. They then moved to the top of the league after beating Rayo Valleanco 1–0 and Real and Atlético both drew 1–1. After beating Las Palmas 0–2, they remained top of the league, level with Real Madrid after 25 matches.

On 25 February, Barcelona faced Atlético Madrid in the Copa Del Rey semi-finals, with the first leg at home. [[Julian Alvarez]] and [[Antoine Griezmann]] scored to put Atlético 0–2 up in 6 minutes, before Pedri, Cubarsí, Martínez and Lewandowski then scored goals to make it 4–2 to Barcelona. However, Atlético scored in the 84th and 93rd minutes as the match ended 4–4, with the second leg to be played away. Three days later, Vitor Roque's loan at Betis was cut short and he completed a permanent move to [[Palmeiras]] for €25.5 million.<ref name="roque2"/>

=== March ===
Barcelona began March by beating Real Sociedad 4–0, with Gerard Martín and [[Marc Casadó]] scoring their first goals for the club, and with Real Madrid losing, they extended their lead at the top of the table to 3 points.

Barcelona faced Benfica in the Champions League round of 16 with the first leg away from home. Raphinha scored the game's only goal to give Barcelona a 0–1 aggregate lead to take to the second leg at home.

On 8 March 2025, Barcelona's scheduled match against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] was postponed roughly 20 minutes prior to kick-off, following the announcement of first-team doctor Carles Miñarro Garcia's death.<ref>{{cite news |date=8 March 2025 |title=Barcelona match postponed after death of team doctor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cjw27xl5236o |access-date=8 March 2025 |website=BBC Sport |archive-date=8 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250308223802/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cjw27xl5236o |url-status=live}}</ref>

Barcelona then won the second leg against Benfica 3–1 at home to advance to the Champions League quarter-finals 4–1 on aggerate. They then came from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2–4 away, putting them level on points with Real Madrid with a game in hand.

Barcelona then won the rearranged fixture against Osasuna 3–0 to move three points clear of the top of the table. they then ended the month by beating Girona 4–1 at home to keep their 3-point lead over Real Madrid.

=== April === 
April began for Barcelona with them beating Atlético Madrid 0–1 away in the Copa Del Rey semi final through a Ferran Torres goal to set up a final with Real Madrid.

Barcelona then drew 1–1 with Real Betis but extended their lead to 4 points after Real Madrid lost their next game.

Barcelona faced [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the Champions League quarter-finals and won the first leg 4–0 at home. Barcelona then beat Leganés 0–1 away to move closer to the title.

Barcelona then lost the second leg of their champions league quarter-finals 3–1 to Dortmund but advanced to the semi-finals 3–5 on aggregate which marked the first time Barcelona had reached the semi-finals since the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|2018–19 edition]].

Barcelona then came from behind to beat Celta Vigo in La Liga 4–3 to remain 4 points clear after Real Madrid won later that week. A 1–0 win over Mallorca from a Dani Olmo goal put Barcelona one step closer to the title.

In the [[2025 Copa del Rey final|Copa Del Rey final]] against Real Madrid, Barcelona won 3–2 after extra time. Pedri opened the scoring for Barcelona in the 23rd minute, but [[Kylian Mbappé]] equalised in the 70th minute to make it 1–1. [[Aurélien Tchouaméni]] scored in the 77th minute to make it 1–2 to Real Madrid, but Ferran Torres scored in the 84th minute to send the match to extra time. Jules Koundé then scored in the 116th minute to win the game for Barcelona giving the Catalan club their 32nd Copa Del Rey title. The match wasn't without controversy, as [[Antonio Rüdiger]] was seen throwing an ice cube at the referee getting a red card, [[Lucas Vázquez]] entered the pitch to confront the referee aggressively and got sent off, and [[Jude Bellingham]] argued with the ref aggressively getting shown a red card. The Copa Del Rey marked Hansi Flick's second trophy as Barcelona manager.

Barcelona ended the month of April by facing [[Inter Milan]] in the Champions League semi-finals. [[Marcus Thuram]] scored in the first minute to give Inter the lead, with [[Denzel Dumfries]] scoring a second in the 21st minute. [[Lamine Yamal]] scored in the 24th minute to bring Barcelona back in the game. Ferran Torres equalised in the 38th minute. Dumfries then made it 2–3 to Inter Milan in the 64th minute, before [[Yann Sommer]] scored an own goal trying to save a Raphinha shot making the score 3–3, which would be the final score.

=== May === 
Barcelona began May by coming from behind to beat Valladolid 1–2, which put them two wins away from the La Liga title. [[Dani Rodríguez (footballer, born 2005)|Dani Rodríguez]] made his debut in the match, starting before being forced off with a shoulder injury.

Barcelona then travelled to the [[San Siro]] to face Inter Milan in the second leg of their Champions League semi-final. [[Lautaro Martínez]] scored in the 21st minute to give Inter the lead. Inter were then awarded a penalty in the 45th minute when Pau Cubarsí tackled Martínez in the box, with [[Hakan Çalhanoğlu]] converting the penalty. The penalty left Hansi Flick furious as Barcelona went into half time 5–3 down on aggregate. Barcelona would fight back with goals from Eric García and Dani Olmo to level the score as they dominated the second half. In the 87th minute, Raphinha had a chance but it was saved by Yann Sommer; however, Raphinha converted the rebound to give Barcelona the lead in the tie for the first time and put them 9 minutes away from a first Champions League final since [[2015 UEFA Champions League final|2015]]. However, in the 6th minute of stoppage time, [[Francesco Acerbi]] scored from a cross from Denzel Dumfries to level the tie despite Barcelona's complaints about a foul in the build up to the goal. The tie finished 6–6 on aggregate, requiring the game to go to extra time. In the 9th minute of extra time, [[Davide Frattesi]] got a cross from Marcus Thuram and fired it into the net to make it 4–3 to Inter and 7–6 on aggregate. Despite two late chances in the seconf half of extra time, Inter held on to win 4–3 and advance to the [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|final]] 7–6 on aggerate. Hansi Flick was furious after the defeat, saying that every 50/50 had gone Inter's way. The semi-final was regarded by pundits and fans as one of the greatest Champions League ties in the history of the competition.

Barcelona then faced Real Madrid at home, knowing a win or draw would put them on the brink of the title. Kylian Mbappé scored a penalty in the 5th minute to give Real Madrid the lead and then added a second goal in the 14th minute. Eric García scored in the 19th minute to reduce the deficit. Lamine Yamal then scored in the 32nd minute to equalise before a Raphinha brace put Barcelona 4–2 up at half time. Mbappé would score a third for Real Madrid in the 70th minute to give them hope, but Barcelona held on to win 4–3 and move 7 points clear of Real Madrid in the title race, meaning a victory against Espanyol would give the Catalan club the league title. This also marked the first time Barcelona won four Clásicos in a season since the [[1982–83 FC Barcelona season|1982–83 campaign]].

Barcelona then faced Espanyol away needing a win to win the title. The game was paused in the 15th minute after a car drove into fans outside the stadium, but resumed after the issue was sorted. The first half finished 0–0, but in the 53rd minute Lamine Yamal scored a brilliant goal to put Barcelona 0–1 up. Fermin López then scored in stoppage time to make it 0–2, confirming the win for Barcelona, which meant the Catalan's won their 28th La Liga title and completed the domestic treble with Hansi Flick winning his third trophy in charge of the club.

Barcelona then suffered a 2–3 home defeat to Villarreal, despite Yamal and López scoring for the 2nd game in a row. The match marked Barcelona's first league defeat since December 2024, and ended a 17-match unbeaten run for the Catalans. Barcelona then won their final game of the season, beating Athletic Bilbao 0–3 with a brace from Lewandowski and a late goal from Olmo to finish with 88 points.

Barcelona ended their season winning the domestic treble, with their only disappointment being the defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League semi-finals. Despite the failure to end their ten-year Champions League drought, this season was arguably most successful for Barcelona since the [[2014–15 FC Barcelona season|2014–15 campaign]]. Due to this, Barcelona extended Hansi Flick's contract until 2027, and gave players like Lamine Yamal and Raphinha new long-term contracts.
